b.x: This is education, not a diagnosis. Insomnia that does not pass, depression, and a wish to die are health. In Brazil, 188 if the wish is to die. 192 if there is already a wound or no breath. Outside Brazil, the number is different. A sleeping tablet, if one exists, is a doctor’s plan, not a page’s.

Sleep is not the brain switched off. It is other work. In deep sleep, what you lived by day is sorted: what matters gains a place, the noise loses priority. It is plasticity without an audience. In the sleep where there is a dream, the load of what hurt is stirred. It does not erase the fact. In many people it lowers the volume at which the fact shouts the next day. Without those shifts, the sad groove does not only continue. It is not filed. It stays on the table, as if it were still now. That is why depression and bad sleep feed each other. One worsens the other. It is not a lack of character. It is a circuit without the night shift.

Without sleep, threat speaks louder and the part that says “this is a thought, not a fact” gets tired. Attention narrows. Hunger and sugar fall out of order. Pain rises. The fuse shortens. The destructive sentence seems more certain precisely because the tired brain lies with more conviction. On the street, that is a reading error: you see an attack where there is hurry, or you do not see what the scene is asking. In the kit, that is a bad decision at three in the morning. No irreversible choice at that hour. The gray man does not treat wakefulness as a medal. Whoever sleeps decides better than whoever poses as tireless.
How much, without becoming a law

Most adults work better near seven to nine hours. A teenager needs more. An older person often sleeps a shorter block and wakes early: that is not a failure, if the day can still think. Your number is the one that leaves the next decision possible, not the app’s. A shift, a small child, and a hot room without air exist. That is not shame. It is a limit. What does not serve is calling sleep what is alcohol: it knocks you out and ruins the deep shift. A short nap, by day, if the night broke, recovers a piece. A long late nap steals the next night. The goal is not heroic bedtime. It is a similar hour on most days, dark, the phone out of the hand.

The same hour to lie down and to get up, also on the free day, within what life allows. Morning light on the face. Coffee early, not at the end of the afternoon. A room that goes dark. The phone charges in another room. The bed is for sleeping, not for the three-in-the-morning court. If the thought does not stop in twenty minutes, get up, one low light, one dull page, and come back when the body weighs. Staying down fighting the mind teaches the mattress to be a battlefield. A walk by day helps the night. The heroic one at eleven does not. If the insomnia is already chronic, the path medicine puts first is sleep therapy, with someone who understands, before a tablet for the rest of life. The plan is the doctor’s.

The neuroplasticity of the day only settles if the night works. Learning something new and not sleeping is leaving the lesson on the floor. Rumination until dawn is rehearsing the sad film at the hour when it should be filed. The role of sleep, in depression and outside it, is this: store what serves, lower the volume of what hurts, give the day back a forehead that tells a thought from a fact. It does not cure alone. Without it, the rest of the treatment works with a blunt tool. Lift your head by day. Lay your head down at night. The two are the same care.
